extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and prospective applicants preparing NIH/NIAID grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Use successful NIH/NIAID sample applications and their summary statements to learn grantsmanship: how to present aims, craft research plans, provide evidence, and address reviewer criteria while following current NIH instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine Specific Aims and Research Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by examining the text sections of the successful example applications—particularly the Specific Aims and Research Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections show how applicants framed the project goals and methodology; use them to observe organization, emphasis, and level of detail. Compare the structure and clarity across samples to identify effective approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare samples with corresponding summary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare each sample with the corresponding summary statement to learn what worked for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary statements to see which parts reviewers praised or criticized and to link specific application language/choices to reviewer reactions. This helps infer why reviewers scored aspects favorably or unfavorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present project goals, plans, and milestones clearly and appealingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask: How did the applicants present project goals, plans, and milestones in an appealing and clear way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concise, well-organized descriptions of aims and realistic, concrete milestones; note tone, framing of significance, and whether timelines and deliverables are explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appropriate evidence and supportive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask: What evidence and support did the applicants provide? How technical were the explanations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the balance between sufficient supporting data/justification and excessive technical detail. Observe how samples provide preliminary data, feasibility arguments, citations, and rationale to support proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address each review criterion effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask: Where and how did the application effectively address each review criterion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map application text to official review criteria (e.g., significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment). Note explicit signposting or sections that directly respond to review criteria and use those patterns in your own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from reviewer-identified strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask: What strong points (or potential weak points) did the reviewers highlight in the summary statements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify concrete strengths to emulate (clear rationale, strong preliminary data, feasible approach) and common weaknesses to avoid. Use reviewer language to understand perceived risks and missing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institute- and mechanism-specific sample collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult available sample applications from relevant NIH institutes and mechanisms (e.g., NIAID Sample Applications, NCI Sample Behavioral Research Grant Applications, NIA K99/R00 samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select samples that match your mechanism (R01, R21, K award, SBIR, etc.) and topical area to get the most relevant examples of structure, emphasis, and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement sample review with official NIH/NIAID guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the samples with advice from NIAID’s Apply for a Grant guidance, NIH’s Important Writing Tips, and NIH’s Write Your Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples demonstrate grantsmanship but should be cross-checked against official guidance to ensure compliance with expected content, organization, and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow current SF 424 instructions and NOFO-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not assume that the samples reflect the latest NIH rules, policies, or format. Always follow the current SF 424 Instructions, notices of NIH Policy Changes, and any other specific instructions listed in your chosen notice of funding opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat older samples as illustrative rather than authoritative; verify formatting, page limits, required attachments, and policy-related elements against the latest official documents to avoid administrative noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about sample currency
rubrics_metrics.description: While sample applications from past years can be a source of valuable grantsmanship lessons, be aware of how much time has passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that policies, forms, and expectations change over time; do not rely on older samples for procedural requirements or recent policy elements. Use them primarily for rhetorical and organizational insight, not as definitive templates.
